evidence.summary: A fixed module-level list of four categories: food, travel, home, other.
Expenses are kept in an in-memory list; nothing is persisted.
add(amount_cents, category, note='') records an expense with an amount in cents, a category and an optional note.
add() rejects a category not in the list with ValueError('unknown category'); the amount is not validated.

architecture.frontend: None: a library function, no user interface.
architecture.backend: One Python module with a module-level category list and an in-memory expense list.

features.name: Add an expense
features.description: Record an expense with an amount in cents, a category and an optional note.
features.observed_behaviour: add() validates the category, then appends a dict {amount_cents, category, note} to an in-memory list.
features.business_logic: Amount in integer minor units (cents) by naming; no currency; amount not validated (negative or non-integer values accepted); note defaults to empty; no id, date or author.
features.integration: Needs persistence, ids, dates and an owner in the unified app.

features.name: Fixed expense categories
features.description: Every expense must use one of four fixed categories: food, travel, home, other.
features.observed_behaviour: CATEGORIES is a constant list; add() raises ValueError('unknown category') for anything else.
features.business_logic: Allowed values exactly food, travel, home, other (lower case, case-sensitive match). No user-defined categories. 'other' is the catch-all.
features.integration: One category vocabulary for every expense, scanned or typed.
